issues.description: Contract mismatch between metadata (PASS/FAIL only) and check (adds MANUAL state)
issues.detail: The PR description and metadata.json specify a two-valued postcondition: PASS for single NIC, FAIL for multiple. The implementation adds a third outcome, MANUAL, for GKE instances. The spec and the code disagree. Either update metadata/description to document MANUAL as part of the contract, or move GKE handling to a muted/allowlist convention rather than inventing a status.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is a leaky, fragile heuristic embedded in the check
issues.detail: Identifying GKE-managed instances via `name.startswith("gke-")` leaks an implementation detail of GKE node naming into a check contract. Users can name instances `gke-*` and the label `goog-gke-node` is the authoritative signal. Add an `is_gke_managed` field to the Instance ADT (derived from labels/metadata in the service) and have the check consume that boolean.

issues.description: Check name and CHANGELOG drift from PR title and stated intent
issues.detail: PR title and feature describe detecting VMs with multiple NICs, but the check, directory, metadata CheckID, and CHANGELOG entry are all `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. The contract should name the predicate it asserts. Pick one (`_multiple_network_interfaces` or `_single_network_interface`) and align CheckID, file paths, class name, and changelog so the spec name matches the check semantics.

issues.description: `network_interfaces` mutable default on Instance model risks shared-state invariant violation
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a mutable default at the class level. Pydantic v1 copies this safely, but the idiomatic and contract-preserving form is `Field(default_factory=list)`. Stating the invariant explicitly (each Instance owns its own list) prevents accidental aliasing if the model migrates or is subclassed.

issues.description: No-NIC branch silently emits PASS with informational message, weakening postcondition
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, the code sets `status_extended` but leaves `status = "PASS"`. The contract for PASS is "single network interface," so zero interfaces violates the stated postcondition. Either treat zero as MANUAL/INFO with an explicit decision, or document that zero-NIC is impossible per the GCP API and assert it.

issues.description: NetworkInterface ADT under-specifies what callers may rely on
issues.detail: `NetworkInterface` exposes `name`, `network`, `subnetwork` as bare strings with empty-string defaults and silently truncates URLs via `split("/")[-1]`. The invariant ("network is the short name, never the self-link") lives only in `_get_instances`. Document it on the model, or make the helper explicit so future callers and subtypes preserve the same postcondition.

review.summary: The check's contract is under-specified and inconsistent with its implementation: metadata promises PASS/FAIL but code emits a third state (MANUAL) for GKE, and the artifact's own name drifts between "single" and "multiple" across PR title, CheckID, and changelog. The GKE carve-out is a leaky abstraction (name-prefix sniffing inside the check) that belongs in the Instance ADT as a derived attribute. The NetworkInterface ADT silently transforms URL self-links and uses a mutable default on Instance, both of which should be stated as invariants rather than implied. Tests cover the happy paths cleanly but never exercise the no-NIC branch, where the postcondition is currently violated.
